THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY. JANUARY 19, 1935 No. 1

HADDON SENTENCED
TO PRISON
Claimed Mother Secretly
Married Duke Of
Clarence

LONDON, Jan. 17.—Clarence
Guy Haddon, at one time a resident
of Shanghai, who was bound over
last January for three years after
pleading guilty to a charge of
uttering letters demanding money
from H. M. the King, with men-
aces, was to-day sentenced at the
Old Bailey to 12 months' imprison-
ment in the second division for
breach of his recognizances.
When the trial opened on Jan-
uary 11; last year, Haddon claim-
ed that he had witnesses to say
that his mother had been secretly
married to the Duke of Clarence.
He was bound over for three years
on his own surety of £100 and two
sureties of £100 each.
In winding up the case, the judge
analyzed the evidence at length.
He asserted that "this is a matter
between yourself and another man.
We do not give consideration to
persons or personalities." He ex-
horted the accused to "get this
maggot out of your brain."—
Reuter.

《字林西报》，星期六，1935年1月19日，第1号

哈顿被判入狱
声称其母曾秘密嫁给
克拉伦斯公爵

伦敦，1月17日电。——克拉伦斯·盖伊·哈顿（Clarence Guy Haddon），前上海居民，去年一月因承认犯有以恐吓手段向国王陛下寄送勒索信件的罪名，被责令具结保释三年，今日在老贝利法院（Old Bailey）因违反具结保释条件，被判处二等监禁十二个月。
在去年1月11日开庭审理时，哈顿声称他有证人可以证明其母亲曾秘密嫁给克拉伦斯公爵。
他被责令具结保释三年，由本人提供100英镑保证金，另有两名担保人各提供100英镑保证金。
在结案陈词中，法官详细分析了证据。他断言：“这是你与另一人之间的事。我们不考虑个人或私人关系。”他告诫被告“把你脑子里的这种妄想清除掉”。——路透社。

R E U T E R
HADDON SENTENCED TO PRISON TERM
CLAIMED MOTHER HAD BEEN SECRETLY MARRIED
TO THE DUKE OF CLARENCE

London, Jan. 17

Clarence Guy Haddon, at one time a resident of Shanghai,
who was bound over last January for three years after
pleading guilty to a charge of uttering letters demanding
money from H. M. the King, with menaces, was to-day
sentenced at the Old Bailey to 12 months' imprisonment in
the second division for breach of his recognisances.

When the trial opened on January 11, last year, Haddon
claimed that he had witnesses to say that his mother had
been secretly married to the Duke of Clarence.
He was bound over for three years on his own surety of
£100 and two sureties of £100 each.

In winding up the case, the judge analysed the evidence
at length. He asserted that "this is a matter between yourself
and another man. We do not give consideration to persons or
personalities." He exhorted the accused to "get this maggot
out of your brain."-Reuter

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 30, 1933

Jailed Briton
Claims To Be
Son Of Royalty

Ex-Shanghai Man Held
For Threatening King
In Plan To Get Money

LONDON, Nov. 29.—(Reuters).—
Mr. Clarence Guy Gordon Haddon,
formerly of H.M. Office of Works,
China, was formally remanded into
custody till December 4 when he
appeared today before the Bow
Street Police Court on a charge of
demanding money by menaces from
the King.
Ball was refused.
Giving evidence, Chief-Inspector
Foster stated that when told of the
charge, Mr. Haddon replied: "This
is the only thing I wanted. I don't
see why I should be hounded about
for being an illegitimate son of the
Duke of Clarence."
Later, added the chief inspector,
Mr. Haddon denied the charge, but
admitted that he had made a petition to the King.
The prosecuting counsel intimated
that it might be desirable to have
a medical report.
Mr. Haddon arrived in Shanghai
from London in November, 1924, to
take up the post of clerk of works
in H.M. Office of Works, Shanghai.
He left Shanghai in December 1926.

《大美晚报》，星期四，1933年11月30日

入狱英人
声称是
皇室之子

前上海男子因
策划勒索国王钱财
并施加威胁而被捕

伦敦，11月29日电。（路透社）。——克拉伦斯·盖伊·戈登·哈顿先生（Mr. Clarence Guy Gordon Haddon），前驻华英国工务局职员，今日在鲍街警察法庭（Bow Street Police Court）出庭，被控以恐吓手段向国王勒索钱财，正式被还押候审至12月4日。
不准保释。
首席督察福斯特（Foster）作证称，当告知哈顿先生所受指控时，他回答说：“这正是我想要的。我不明白为什么仅仅因为我是克拉伦斯公爵的私生子就要受到迫害。”
首席督察补充说，后来哈顿先生否认了该项指控，但承认他曾向国王递交请愿书。
公诉律师暗示，可能需要一份医学报告。
哈顿先生于1924年11月从伦敦抵达上海，就任英国驻上海工务局工程监工一职。
他于1926年12月离开上海。
